```{r readdata, echo = F, include = F}
# load data set
empro <- here::here("data", "EMPRO_data_20260408.RData")
load(empro)

#make enrollment month factor 
empro_data$enrollment_month1 = factor(empro_data$enrollment_month)

#make new variable for yes/no CRPC
empro_data$crpc_per = empro_data$cohort_empro != "mHSPC"

# add variable for not matched
empro_data$not_matched = ifelse(empro_data$subject %in% not_matched, 1, 0)

#relabel new vars
var_label(empro_data) <- list(
  crpc_per = "CRPC (vs. mHSPC)", 
  enrollment_month1 = "Study visit at entry")

# read in site-level data
site_data <- read.csv("H:/GU/EMPRO/Randomization/randscheme_final.csv") %>% 
  rename(site_country = Country,
         site_timetodx = timetodx,
         site_crpc = CRPC)

# analysis data set (remove exclusions)
analysis_data <- empro_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(empro_cnstdate) & enrollment_month<=45 & !is.na(cohort_empro)) %>%
  mutate(enrollment_month1 = fct_drop(enrollment_month1)) %>%
  mutate(sitenew = case_when(
    site=="Cross Cancer Institute (Alberta Health Services)" ~ "Cross Cancer Institute",
    site=="Guys St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust" ~ "Guys and St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust",
    site=="Royal Brisbane & Women’s Hospital" ~ "Royal Brisbane & Women's Hospital",
    site=="St. Vincent’s Hospital Sydney" ~ "St. Vincent's Hospital Sydney",
    site=="University of Virgina (UVA)" ~ "University of Virginia", 
    site=="Royal Brisbane & Women's Hospital" ~ "Queensland University of Technology",
    site=="NewYork-Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital" ~ "Weill Cornell Medical Center",
    TRUE ~ site),
    ecog3 = replace_na(ecog2, "Unknown")) %>% 
  left_join(site_data, by = c("sitenew"="sitegp")) %>% 
  mutate(# re-order - this matches the order from when they were randomized (must match constrained space file)
    sitenew = factor(sitenew,
                           levels = c("Queensland University of Technology",
                                      "Eastern Health",
                                      "St. Vincent's Hospital Sydney",
                                      "Macquarie University Hospital",
                                      "Cross Cancer Institute",
                                      "Ottawa Hospital Cancer Centre",
                                      "The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust",
                                      "Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust",
                                      "Guys and St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust",
                                      "University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust",
                                      "Duke Comprehensive Cancer Center",
                                      "Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center",
                                      "Weill Cornell Medical Center",
                                      "University of Virginia")),
    eortc_0_log = log(max(eortc_0, na.rm=TRUE) + 1 - eortc_0)) %>% 
  set_variable_labels(ecog3="ECOG",
                      enrollment_month1 = "Study visit at entry")

# complete data at 6 mo
analysis_data2 <- analysis_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(eortc_6)) 

# narrow down dataset to only needed variables
to_impute <- analysis_data %>% 
  select(eortc_6, arm, ecog2, race_gp, educ_gp, crpc_per, sitenew)

# patient counts
n_crpc <- analysis_data %>% filter(cohort=="CRPC" & arm=="intervention") %>% nrow()
n_mhspc <- analysis_data %>% filter(cohort=="mHSPC" & arm=="intervention") %>% nrow()
n_intervention <- analysis_data %>% filter(arm=="intervention") %>% nrow()

```

# Permutation test
Complete case analysis

## Unadjusted
Only adjusted for subject-level covariates
```{r}
# should be:
#                                             clustername allocation
# 1                   Queensland University of Technology          0
# 2                                        Eastern Health          1
# 3                         St. Vincent's Hospital Sydney          0
# 4                         Macquarie University Hospital          1
# 5                                Cross Cancer Institute          1
# 6                         Ottawa Hospital Cancer Centre          0
# 7                The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust          0
# 8    Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust          0
# 9              Guys and St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust          1
# 10 University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust          1
# 11                     Duke Comprehensive Cancer Center          0
# 12               Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center          1
# 13                         Weill Cornell Medical Center          1
# 14                               University of Virginia          0

cptest(outcome = analysis_data2$eortc_6,
       clustername = analysis_data2$sitenew,
       z = data.frame(analysis_data2[ , c("age_baseline", "ecog3", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "crpc_per")]), 
       cspacedatname = "H:/GU/EMPRO/Randomization/empro_constrained.csv",
       outcometype = "continuous",                                                      
       categorical = c("ecog3", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "crpc_per"))

```

# F-test
## Unadjusted
Only adjusted for subject-level covariates
```{r}
# linear mixed model
fit <- lmer(eortc_6 ~ arm + age_baseline + ecog3 + race_gp + educ_gp + crpc_per + 
              (1 | sitenew), data = analysis_data2, REML = TRUE)

# Type-III ANOVA table with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom
anova_Satt <- anova(fit, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite")
anova_Satt
# Look for the row 'trt' → gives F-statistic and p-value for the treatment effect

# estimate ICC
isSingular(fit, tol = 1e-5)
summary(fit)
VarCorr(fit) # Var(site) ≈ 0 → indicates negligible ICC.


# estimate icc
vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit))
vc$vcov[vc$grp == "sitenew"] / sum(vc$vcov) # If ICC ≈ 0, the warning is expected and not necessarily a problem—your data simply don’t support an extra random‐effect variance.


```

## Adjusted
Adjusted for subject-level covariates and site-level covariates included in the randomization scheme (measured at the time of randomization).
```{r}
# linear mixed model
fit_adj <- lmer(eortc_6 ~ arm + age_baseline + ecog3 + race_gp + educ_gp + crpc_per + 
              site_country + site_timetodx + site_crpc +
              (1 | sitenew), data = analysis_data2, REML = TRUE)
# singular warning: random-effect variance for sitenew is estimated ≈ 0 in many imputations.

# Type-III ANOVA table with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom
anova_Satt <- anova(fit_adj, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite")
anova_Satt
# Look for the row 'trt' → gives F-statistic and p-value for the treatment effect

# estimate ICC
isSingular(fit_adj, tol = 1e-5)
summary(fit_adj)
VarCorr(fit_adj) # Var(site) ≈ 0 → indicates negligible ICC.


# estimate icc
vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit_adj))
vc$vcov[vc$grp == "sitenew"] / sum(vc$vcov) # If ICC ≈ 0, the warning is expected and not necessarily a problem—your data simply don’t support an extra random‐effect variance.


```

## With imputation
```{r}
# This was a test case for missing at random that works but is not weighted by performance status
# there is an association between ECOG and missingness of EORTC
chisq.test(analysis_data$ecog3, is.na(analysis_data$eortc_6))


# --- Multiple imputation
imp <- mice(to_impute, m = 20, maxit = 10, seed = 123, method = c(eortc_6="pmm", ecog2="polyreg", arm="", race_gp="", educ_gp="", crpc_per="", sitenew=""))
# - pmm: Predictive mean matching (numeric)
# - norm: Bayesian linear regression (numeric)
# - logreg: Logistic regression (factor, 2 categories)
# - polyreg: Polytomous (unordered) regression (factor, >= 2 categories)

# apply function to imputed data
fit_list <- with(imp, lme4::lmer(eortc_6 ~ arm + ecog2 + race_gp + educ_gp + crpc_per + (1|sitenew), REML = FALSE))

# Pool without broom
pooled <- pool(fit_list)

# Summarize and convert to tibble safely
res <- summary(pooled, conf.int = TRUE)

res_tibble <- tibble::as_tibble(res) |>
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 3)))

res_tibble

```

### Adjusting for MNAR
```{r, eval = FALSE}
# compare survival by ECOG
tbl_survfit(
    survfit(Surv(limbo, dead) ~ ecog3, analysis_data),
    times = c(12, 24),
    label_header = "**{time} Month**"
)
# missing ECOG has poor prognosis

## =========================
## MNAR imputation for EORTC (continuous) using NARFCS (delta-adjustment)
## with stronger negative shifts for worse ECOG and for missing ECOG
## =========================

# ECOG: create indicators that are robust to factor/numeric storage and NAs
ecog_chr <- as.character(to_impute$ecog2)  # handles factor or numeric gracefully
to_impute$ecog_missing <- as.integer(is.na(to_impute$ecog2))
to_impute$ecog1        <- as.integer(!is.na(to_impute$ecog2) & ecog_chr == "1")
to_impute$ecog2_hi     <- as.integer(!is.na(to_impute$ecog2) & ecog_chr == "2-4")

# --- 2) Build method and predictor matrices for mice
meth <- make.method(to_impute)
pred <- make.predictorMatrix(to_impute)

# We will MNAR-impute EORTC; other variables stay as-is ("" = not imputed)
meth["eortc_6"] <- "mnar.norm"

# IMPORTANT: the ECOG indicators are used only in the MNAR (unidentifiable) part,
# not in the identifiable MAR model. So exclude them from the predictor matrix:
pred[, c("ecog_missing", "ecog1", "ecog2_hi")] <- 0
pred[c("ecog_missing", "ecog1", "ecog2_hi"), ] <- 0

# --- 3) Specify the MNAR (NARFCS) 'blots' for eortc_6
# Delta specification (tune these for sensitivity):
#   ECOG missing  -> -5
#   ECOG level 1  -> -3
#   ECOG level 2  -> -6
#   ECOG level 0  ->  0  (no indicator turns on)
umx_df <- data.frame(
  ecog_missing = to_impute$ecog_missing,
  ecog1        = to_impute$ecog1,
  ecog2_hi     = to_impute$ecog2_hi
)

blots <- list(
  eortc_6 = list(
    # You can add + rnorm(1,0,1) at the end for extra uncertainty
    ums = "0 + -5*ecog_missing + -3*ecog1 + -6*ecog2_hi",
    umx = umx_df
  )
)

# --- 4) Run MNAR imputation (NARFCS)
set.seed(2026)
imp_mnar <- mice(
  to_impute,
  m               = 20,   # number of imputations
  maxit           = 15,   # iterations
  method          = meth,
  predictorMatrix = pred,
  blots           = blots,
  printFlag       = TRUE
)

# --- 5) Quick diagnostics
print(imp_mnar)
# Visualize distributions of imputed eortc_6
# (Uncomment if you want plots)
# stripplot(imp_mnar, eortc_6)
# densityplot(imp_mnar, ~ eortc_6)

# --- 6) Extract completed datasets
# Single completed dataset:
comp1 <- complete(imp_mnar, action = 1)

# All completed datasets as a list:
all_sets <- lapply(seq_len(imp_mnar$m), function(i) complete(imp_mnar, action = i))

# --- 7) (Optional) Fit your mixed model across imputations
# IMPORTANT: Inside with(imp, ...), refer to the dataset as 'data' or directly fit the model.
fit_list <- with(
  imp_mnar,
  lmer(eortc_6 ~ arm + ecog2 + race_gp + educ_gp + crpc_per + (1 | sitenew),
       REML = FALSE)
)

# --- 8) (Optional) Pooled test for treatment arm using Rubin's rules
# Use D1() for a pooled Wald/F-test. You must pass the exact coefficient name(s).
# First, inspect the coefficient names from one imputed model:
coef_names <- names(fixef(fit_list$analyses[[1]]))
print(coef_names)

# If 'arm' is binary, you might see something like "armB" or "armTreatment".
# Replace "armB" below with the actual name in your model:
# Example for binary arm:
# pooled_test <- D1(fit_list, terms = "armB")

# If 'arm' has >2 levels, jointly test all associated coefficients, e.g. c("armB","armC"):
# pooled_test <- D1(fit_list, terms = c("armB","armC"))
# print(pooled_test)

# --- 9) (Optional) Pooled coefficient table without depending on broom
# If your mice version is old and pool(..., use.broom = FALSE) is unavailable, you can still summarize each model:
# Summaries per imputation:
# per_imp <- lapply(fit_list$analyses, function(mod) summary(mod)$coef)
# names(per_imp) <- paste0("imp", seq_along(per_imp))
# str(per_imp)

```
